content:
MRI BREAST BILATERAL - RESPONSE ASSESSMENT

Patient: [redacted], MRN [redacted], DOB [redacted]
Study date: [redacted]
Performed in: [redacted]

AN ADDENDUM HAS BEEN ENTERED AT THE END OF THIS REPORT

Clinical details: Right breast IDC grade 3, ER0 PR0 HER2 3+. Biopsy-proven right axillary nodal disease. Mid-treatment assessment following 4 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Previous left breast WLE and adjuvant radiotherapy 2019 for DCIS. Previous pulmonary embolism on apixaban.

Comparison: staging MRI [redacted], prior to commencement of systemic therapy.

Technique: MRI both breasts with IV gadolinium. Dedicated breast coil. Motion artefact on the early dynamic sequences degrades assessment of the retroareolar region; repeat delayed sequences were acquired and are diagnostic.

Findings:

Fibroglandular pattern: ACR C - heterogeneously dense.
BPE: Mild.

RIGHT BREAST:
The known index mass in the lower outer quadrant has reduced, now measuring 31 x 24 x 20mm (previously 52 x 44 x 38mm). It remains an irregular, spiculated, avidly enhancing mass with central necrosis, lying 14mm deep to the skin surface. This is the designated target lesion for response assessment. Previously described dermal invasion is no longer evident; the overlying skin thickening has resolved and there is no residual skin nodularity.

The associated non-mass enhancement extending superiorly into the upper outer quadrant has reduced from 28mm to 11mm in craniocaudal extent. This remains malignant enhancement contiguous with the index mass.

A 5mm focus of enhancement in the right upper inner quadrant shows benign kinetics and is favoured to represent a focus of fibrocystic change. This is unchanged from the staging study and is not considered suspicious.

RIGHT AXILLA:
The largest level 1 node has reduced from 32mm to 17mm in short axis, with partial restoration of the fatty hilum. Level 2 nodes have reduced to below 10mm. The level 3 / apical node measures 9mm and remains indeterminate.

LEFT BREAST:
Post-surgical seroma and architectural distortion in the left upper outer quadrant, in keeping with the previous wide local excision. Associated skin thickening consistent with prior radiotherapy change. Stable. No suspicious enhancement.

IMC:
No internal mammary lymphadenopathy.

Impression:
1. Good partial response of the right breast index mass and associated NME to neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
2. Resolution of previously demonstrated dermal invasion.
3. Substantial response of right axillary nodal disease. Apical node remains indeterminate.
4. Stable post-treatment change in the left breast.

RCR: Right MRI 6, Left MRI 2

ADDENDUM START
On review at the breast MDT, the right level 3 / apical node demonstrates persistent cortical thickening on the delayed sequences and is considered to represent residual nodal disease rather than an indeterminate node.

output.report_summary: Mid-treatment breast MRI after 4 cycles of neoadjuvant chemotherapy shows good partial response of the right lower outer quadrant index mass (31mm from 52mm, target lesion) and of the associated non-mass enhancement (11mm from 28mm), with resolution of previously demonstrated dermal invasion. Right axillary nodal disease has responded substantially; per addendum the level 3 apical node represents residual nodal disease. Stable post-surgical and post-radiotherapy change in the left breast. RCR right MRI 6, left MRI 2; ACR density C. A 5mm right upper inner quadrant focus was favoured benign and excluded.
